harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built and verified the three-node Redis/Sentinel service. Node1 began as primary; controlled failure promoted node2, and node1 returned as a synchronized replica. Final topology is node2 primary with node1/node3 replicas. Redis and Sentinel require mutual TLS plus authentication, `infra:proof=ready` persists, and all three nodes passed sequential OS-reboot recovery.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled Redis 7 and Sentinel on all nodes.
Configured unique CA-signed node certificates, TLS-only listeners, ACL authentication, AOF persistence, and three-Sentinel quorum for `infra-primary`.
Created root-owned mode-0600 administrative credentials at `/root/redis-admin.env` on node1.
Demonstrated automatic failover and synchronized former-primary recovery.
Safely rebooted node1, node3, and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and full recovery after each.

evidence.requirement: Initial node1 primary with node2/node3 synchronized replicas
evidence.summary: Node1 reported master with two connected replicas; node2 and node3 reported replica links up to node1.

evidence.requirement: Three Sentinels monitor infra-primary with quorum
evidence.summary: Every Sentinel discovered two peers and two replicas and reported three usable Sentinels with failover authorization available.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated TLS on Redis 6379 and Sentinel 26379
evidence.summary: Each node proves plaintext is blocked, client certificates are required, unauthenticated clients are rejected, authenticated TLS returns PONG, Redis plaintext port is disabled, and certificates validate.
`/root/redis-admin.env` is nonempty, root-owned mode 0600, and contains Redis, Sentinel, authentication, and TLS path variables.
The write received two replica acknowledgements, and every node returned `ready` after failover and all reboots.
Only node1 Redis was stopped; Sentinel promoted node2, node2 served and replicated data, and restored node1 rejoined node2 with link up and outage-period data present.
Healthy baseline and original boot ID, safe-reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, direct recovery, persisted data, replica synchronization, listeners, and quorum are proven.
Healthy baseline and original boot ID, safe-reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, direct recovery, persisted data, replica synchronization, listeners, and quorum are proven.
Healthy primary baseline and original boot ID, safe-reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovery as primary with two connected replicas, persisted data, listeners, and quorum are proven.

Final direct checks show active/enabled services, AOF and TLS replication enabled, node2 primary, node1/node3 synchronized replicas, no down/disconnected members, two peers per Sentinel, and full quorum.
